c.tagline: Storybook karst peaks and the Li River cruise to Yangshuo.

taxi.fareNote: Metered from about ¥9-11; airport and long trips are often a negotiated flat rate. Pay by Alipay/WeChat or cash.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 120 an ambulance, and 119 the fire service; there is no single combined emergency number, and 112 works from mobiles to route you.

avoid.reason: Watch for overpriced 'tea ceremony' invitations, pushy tour touts and inflated taxi fares around Elephant Trunk Hill and the train stations.

hood_desc: The compact heart of Guilin around Central Square, the Zhengyang pedestrian street, and Solitary Beauty Peak, ringed by the Two Rivers Four Lakes waterways; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers, with restaurants, shops, and evening lake cruises at the door.
Named for Elephant Trunk Hill, Guilin's emblem, this riverside district hugs the Li River just south of the center and puts the city's signature karst scenery and best photo spots on the doorstep.
The northern district around Folded Brocade Hill and Fubo Hill, offering classic river-and-peak panoramas and a quieter, greener feel a short ride from downtown.
East of the Li River around Seven Star Park, Guilin's largest green space, a calmer, more residential area good for families and travelers who want parks and room to breathe.
lodging: Guilin Yifang Landscape Lijiang Beauty Hotel

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:30 PM; there are no metro or tram lines.
transit.note: Guilin has no metro; an extensive city bus network (including tourist lines to the main parks) plus taxis and DiDi cover the compact center, and most sights are walkable or a short ride apart.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning an Alipay or WeChat Pay QR code, tapping a rechargeable Guilin transit card, or cash (exact change, flat ¥1-2 fare) on board.

bus: Intercity coaches to Yangshuo, Longsheng, and around Guangxi

car.idp: Not valid — China does not recognize the International Driving Permit; a temporary Chinese driving permit is required to drive.

ferry: Li River tourist cruise boats (Guilin to Yangshuo)
train: Guilin Railway Station, Guilin North and Guilin West Stations (high-speed rail to Guangzhou, Nanning, and Guiyang)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to the city center / railway station (~60 min)
Taxi to the city center (40-60 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in China; no service charge or gratuity is needed at restaurants, hotels, or taxis.

food.name: Guilin Rice Noodles
food.desc: Guilin mifen: round rice noodles under braised beef, pickled long beans, fried peanuts and scallion, served dry with a spoonful of aromatic stock brine.

places.name: Chongshan Rice Noodles
places.note: Serving since 1986 with several city-center branches; the local benchmark for mifen.

places.name: Zhengyang Pedestrian Street shops
places.note: Row of noodle windows in the main walking street; convenient and open through the day.

places.name: West Street noodle shops
places.note: Yangshuo's own versions, usually with English menus and a milder chili hand.

food.name: Yangshuo Beer Fish
food.desc: Li River carp pan-fried skin-on, then braised with beer, tomato, peppers and perilla. The scales are left on for a crisp edge and no muddy taste.

places.name: Master Chef Beer Fish
places.note: Won the local beer-fish championship; several branches, clean rooms, consistent cooking.

places.name: Cloud 9 Restaurant
places.note: Long popular with locals and visitors alike for beer fish and the wider Guangxi menu.

places.name: Li River bankside restaurants
places.note: Casual river-view kitchens cooking the day's catch; agree the fish price by weight first.

food.name: Stuffed River Snails
food.desc: Niang tian luo: field snails emptied, chopped with pork and mint, packed back into their shells and simmered in peppery broth. Sucked straight from the shell.

places.name: Cloud 9 Restaurant
places.note: Reliable version of a dish that is easy to get wrong; explains it well to first-timers.

places.name: Jimo Bamboo Rice Restaurant
places.note: Known for field snails and Li River shrimp alongside its bamboo-tube rice.

places.name: Yangshuo West Street stalls
places.note: Snack stands selling snails by the bowl in the evening; the cheapest way to try them.

food.name: Bamboo Rice and Stuffed Vegetables
food.desc: Rice steamed inside a green bamboo tube, plus the local niang cai family: tofu, chilies and gourds stuffed with minced pork and steamed.

places.name: Jimo Bamboo Rice Restaurant
places.note: Named for the dish; the bamboo is split open at the table and eaten with river dishes.

places.name: Cloud 9 Restaurant
places.note: Good place to sample several different stuffed vegetables in one order.

food.name: Taro-Braised Pork
food.desc: Lipu yu tou kou rou: alternating slices of fried pork belly and Lipu taro steamed with fermented bean sauce until both melt. A Guangxi banquet centerpiece.

places.name: Zhengyang Street restaurants
places.note: Sit-down restaurants along the walking street list it as a house specialty.

places.name: Cloud 9 Restaurant
places.note: One of the easier places to order it as a single dish rather than a banquet portion.

food.name: Li River Shrimp
food.desc: Tiny freshwater prawns flash-fried whole with garlic and chili until the shells crisp, then eaten head and all. Often served with Guilin chili sauce.

places.name: Jimo Bamboo Rice Restaurant
places.note: Li River shrimp is a recommended dish here, cooked to order from the river catch.

places.name: Riverside restaurants
places.note: Best where the boats land; ask what came in that morning.

food.name: Guilin Sanhua Jiu
food.desc: Three Flower Wine: a clear rice spirit distilled with Li River water and aged in the hillside caves of Elephant Trunk Hill. Strong, clean and famously local.

places.name: Zhengyang Pedestrian Street shops
places.note: Specialty stores sell it in every size from tasting cups to ceramic jars.

places.name: Local restaurants citywide
places.note: Poured in small cups with dinner; ask for sanhua rather than generic baijiu.

food.name: Osmanthus Tea and Wine
food.desc: Guilin means forest of osmanthus. The blossoms are dried for a honeyed floral tea, or steeped into a sweet golden wine best drunk in autumn.

places.name: Zhengyang Street tea shops
places.note: Sell dried osmanthus, osmanthus green tea and bottled guihua wine; tastings are common.

places.name: Yangshuo West Street shops
places.note: Convenient for small bottles as gifts, though prices are higher than in the city.

landmarks: Li River (Lijiang) Cruise to Yangshuo
Drifting past mist-wrapped karst pinnacles, water buffalo and bamboo rafts, this legendary river journey is the definitive image of southern China's landscape painting come alive.
Elephant Trunk Hill (Xiangbishan)
Guilin's beloved symbol, a limestone hill shaped like an elephant drinking from the Li River, frames a moonlit arch photographed by every visitor to the city.
Reed Flute Cave (Ludi Yan)
A 240-meter cavern of rainbow-lit stalactites and stone curtains dubbed the Palace of Natural Arts, wowing travelers with subterranean spectacle for over a millennium.
Longji Rice Terraces (Longsheng, Dragon's Backbone)
Two hours from Guilin, these 650-year-old terraces cascade down mountainsides like dragon scales, tended by Zhuang and Yao villagers in traditional dress.
Sun and Moon Pagodas (Riyue Shuang Ta)
Twin pagodas of gold and silver rise from Shanhu Lake, connected by an underwater tunnel and gloriously reflected in Guilin's Two Rivers and Four Lakes at night.
Seven Star Park (Qixing Gongyuan)
Guilin's largest park bundles karst peaks, the Flower Bridge, Seven Star Cave and Camel Hill into a leafy riverside retreat right in the city center.
Fubo Hill (Wave-Subduing Hill)
A riverside crag honeycombed with Buddhist carvings and the Sword-Testing Rock, its summit terrace offers one of the finest close-up panoramas of downtown Guilin's karst skyline.
Diecai Hill (Folded Brocade Hill)
Layered limestone strata resembling folded silk give this hill its name, with Ming-era carvings, the breezy Wind Cave and sunset views across the Li River.
Jingjiang Princes' Palace and Solitary Beauty Peak
A Ming-dynasty princely palace older than Beijing's Forbidden City encloses Duxiu Feng, the sheer Solitary Beauty Peak whose stairway climbs to imperial views.
Xingping Ancient Town
This 1,300-year-old fishing town on the Li River fronts the exact karst panorama printed on China's 20-yuan banknote, best admired from a sunrise riverside stroll.

train.note: Guilin has no international trains, though the sleeper coach to Hanoi covers that gap. Guilin North and Guilin West handle the high-speed services and are both some way out of town, while the central Guilin station is the most convenient for the hotels; Nanning is about 3 hours, Guangzhou and Shenzhen 2.5-3.5 hours, and there are through services to Kunming, Xi'an, Chengdu and Hong Kong, with conventional trains from Beijing still taking around 30 hours. Book on 12306 with your passport and check carefully which of the three stations your ticket shows.

intl.to: Hanoi (Vietnam) - overnight sleeper coach via the Youyi Guan / Friendship Pass crossing
intl.op: cross-border sleeper coach, tickets at Guilin bus terminal counters or through 12Go

bus.note: The main Guilin bus terminal is on Zhongshan Nanlu just north of the railway station, with buses to Nanning, Kunming, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Zhuhai, and constant minibuses to and from Yangshuo for about ¥18. A daily sleeper coach leaves in the evening for Hanoi, costs around ¥390 and takes most of the night - sort out a Vietnamese visa or e-visa before you travel, because nothing is issued at the border. Domestic tickets are sold at the counters and on Chinese apps; cross-border seats are easiest to arrange a day or two ahead at the terminal.

intl.to: Yangshuo (China) - Li River cruise boats from the piers at Zhujiang and Mopanshan, about an hour south of Guilin
intl.op: Li River cruise services (tickets via Ctrip or Guilin travel agents)

ferry.note: The Li River cruise to Yangshuo is the classic way out of Guilin: boats board at Zhujiang or Mopanshan pier, leave mid-morning and take four to four and a half hours downstream through the karst scenery. There are no passenger boats back upstream, so you return to Guilin by bus or train, and in the dry winter months low water can shorten the route or push you onto a bamboo raft section instead. Cargo boats occasionally take passengers from Wuzhou to Yangshuo for very little, but they are slow and not a scheduled service.

half.name: Silver Cave (Yinzi Yan)
half.blurb: Limestone cavern south of the city with illuminated stalactite chambers and an underground lake, among Guangxi's largest karst caves.

half.name: Gudong Waterfall
half.blurb: Multi-tiered waterfall in a forested gorge, reached by a short hike along the Gudong River.

half.name: Yao Mountain
half.blurb: Highest peak on Guilin's outskirts, climbed by cable car or chairlift for views over the karst hills and Li River.

full.name: Ziyuan Hot Springs
full.blurb: Mountain hot spring resort in northern Guangxi, with mineral pools set among forested slopes.

full.name: Rongshui Miao Autonomous County
full.blurb: Miao and Dong minority county with terraced hillsides, wooden drum towers, and traditional villages.
